newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Coffee falls as weather, crop concerns ease.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Coffee falls as weather, crop concerns ease.

text.p: World coffee prices fell on Thursday as investors sold off their positions against a background of reduced fears over Brazilian weather or the size of the world number one producer's crop.
Elsewhere, recently volatile metal markets calmed down but Chicago grain markets remained sensitive to weather reports.
On the London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE) the September coffee futures position lost $35 to stand at $1,636 a tonne.

Trade sources said a small threat of a cold weather front moving up to the Brazilian coffee belt had been removed when private U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said it does not appear strong enough to penetrate that far.
Also, recent market talk that the Brazilian Government was about to reduce its crop estimate was denied by the interim head of the National Coffee Department.
"Despite the private sector predicting a crop as low as 18 million bags, we stick to our projection of a crop of 22 million bags," Roberto Abreu said.
On the Chicago Board of Trade prices for soyabean romped ahead on active demand for remaining old crop supplies prompted by concerns that hot, dry weather would hurt the new crop.
"When you've got a threat to the new crop, the old crop becomes that much more valuable,' one Chicago trader said.
The remaining old crop position, August, rose 10 cents to $7.66 a bushel which was 85 cents above September new crop.
Wheat and corn markets, although relatively calm, kept one eye on the weather, both rising about three cents a bushel by midday.
On the London Metal Exchange this week's volatility was much reduced and traders reckoned the markets were looking for some sort of consolidation action.

The zinc market which has been a particularly wide mover beacause of heavy Chinese involvement actually finished Thursday trading unchanged from the previous day's close, and other metals showed relatively small movements.
